tagline: Exploratory testing that finds what your scripts never thought to try
intro: We are a small team of exploratory testers. We spend timed sessions inside your product the way a curious, impatient customer would, and write up everything we notice in notes your developers can act on.
audience: Software teams in the UK and Ireland building web apps, mobile apps and internal tools, especially those with some automated tests but nobody paid to wander off the happy path.
pricing_note: Sessions are sold in blocks of ten, each ninety minutes with a written debrief. Most teams start with one block before a release and add more as they need them.

services.title: Exploratory sessions
services.description: Ninety-minute sessions against a written charter, such as new users on a slow phone. You get timestamped notes, bugs with steps and the questions we could not answer.

services.title: Release bug bashes
services.description: Two days before a release, several of us explore the new build together and triage what we find with your team at the end of each day.

services.title: Journey walkthroughs
services.description: We follow your most important journeys from first visit to repeat use and note every place a real person would hesitate, get it wrong or give up.

services.title: Test notes for your team
services.description: We turn what we learned into short, readable checklists your own team can rerun before each release, without needing a testing background.

process.title: Write the charter
process.description: We agree with you what each session explores and why: an area, a kind of user, a risk you are worried about. One charter per session, on a single page.

process.title: Explore and take notes
process.description: A tester works through the charter for ninety minutes, logging what they tried, what happened and anything that looked wrong, with timestamps.

process.title: Debrief the same day
process.description: A short call to walk your team through the notes. Bugs go into your tracker with steps; open questions go to whoever can answer them.

proof.text: The session notes read like a customer thinking aloud. Our designers asked for them too.
proof.source: Product lead, an Edinburgh property software company (sample)

proof.text: They found three ways to get stuck in onboarding in the first ninety minutes.
The checklists they left behind are now part of our release routine.
